title: Adaptive Reservation Lab: Sprint-based commitment sync & autoscale recovery experimentation
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Objective: run a focused experiment series to validate a sprint-based reservation cadence that minimizes overcommit while retaining predictable burst capacity and fast autoscale recovery. We will treat the initiative as a lab: define 3 commitment window variants, exercise them with traffic replays and chaos recovery, and produce deterministic rollout criteria for Dedicated pools. Background: teams have repeatedly traded long reservation windows for safety, which increases cost. Hypothesis: a short cadence (1–2 week commit windows) with prewarm + rapid autoscale recovery sequences can reduce committed spend by 12–20% on test workloads while keeping P95 latency within SLOs and maintaining customer success for tiered SLAs. Scope: dedicated pool experiments, runtime autoscale playbooks, recovery sequences, billing estimate modeling, and rollout gating (metrics, safety checks). Out of scope: changes to pricing model or new SKUs (those will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Three commitment window variants defined and documented (1-week, 2-week, rolling-4-week) with explicit prewarm and teardown rules
Traffic replay harness configured for two representative customers and synthetic burst traces
Autoscale recovery workflow implemented in staging with <60s median recovery to baseline throughput for at least 90% of trials
Economic model showing projected committed spend delta vs baseline for each variant, with assumptions and sensitivity analysis
Runbook and canary gating checklist approved by capacity-ops and infra oncall
A recommended rollout plan (canary -> ramp -> global) with quantitative abort conditions
tasks: Design experiment matrix and success metrics
Implement traffic replay and failure-replay harness (ENG)
Build autoscale recovery sequence and prewarm API endpoints (ENG)
Run economic simulation and update pricing model assumptions (PM/Finance)
Define canary gating checklist and runbook (SRE + Capacity Ops)
Execute lab runs, collect telemetry, and analyze results
Prepare rollout proposal and stakeholder review doc
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng, SRE, and Finance. Agreed on three variants and primary metrics (P95 latency, cost delta, recovery time). Action: ENG to prototype replay harness.

2026-03-04: Prototype replay harness committed to feature-branch. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-replay/pull/142. Eng notes: initial KV cache warm path needs optimization to avoid warmup noise.

2026-03-06: Finance provided baseline spend profile for two pilot customers. Early model shows 10–18% upside on committed cost by shifting to 2-week windows for bursty customers. Follow-up: sensitivity runs for 30–50% burst intensity.

2026-03-07: Design review with Capacity Ops. Agreed on canary gating: (1) P95 <= 1.2x historical SLO, (2) recovery median <= 60s, (3) cost delta <= target range. Capacity Ops requested abort paths to fallback to reserved baseline within 15 minutes.
2026-03-08: Blocker identified: private deployment telemetry for prewarm success is noisy. ENG assigned sub-issue ENG-22567 to improve prewarm signal and add end-to-end assert.
2026-03-08: Draft runbook uploaded to Confluence and linked for review. Next: schedule run with pilot customers for week of 2026-03-15.
success_metrics: Committed spend reduction vs baseline (primary): target 12% for pilot cohort
Tail latency P95 during burst: <= 1.2x historical SLO
Customer-reported degradation incidents: 0 in pilot cohort (severity >= P1)
risks_mitigation: Risk: Prewarm failures cause customer-visible latency. Mitigation: require prewarm success assertion and fallback to reserved baseline within 15 minutes.
Risk: Economic model assumptions wrong for long-tail customers. Mitigation: conservative sensitivity analysis and holdback 10% capacity to absorb variance.
Risk: Billing edge-cases for short reservation windows. Mitigation: coordinate with Billing team to simulate invoices and flag disputes early.
Risk: SRE bandwidth for canary. Mitigation: schedule weekday runs and automate alerting for pre-specified abort conditions.
